images.title: Physical encoding on a historical punched card
images.summary: A digitized 80-column IBM-standard punched card, showing how human information can be stored as the presence or absence of holes at defined positions.
images.alt: Pink rectangular card with printed rows of digits and rectangular punched holes.
images.caption: A historical example of information encoded in physical material. Reading the holes as characters requires a convention. This is not Centauri Archive's proposed 8-by-8 engraved plate, which remains an unmanufactured research deliverable.
images.rights: CC BY-SA 3.0, Harke; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/. Archive derivative retains the same license.
images.processing: Source documentary image converted by the archive importer to an orientation-corrected JPEG, maximum 1800 pixels, quality 87. No synthetic content or compositional changes. Original source retained by URL.

images.title: Preparing humanity's Golden Record for interstellar travel
images.summary: NASA archival photograph documenting preparation of the Voyager Golden Record in 1977.
images.alt: A gloved cleanroom worker holds a gold-colored record beside a second circular metal component on a covered table.
images.caption: The Voyager mission carried recorded images and sounds from Earth into interstellar space. This photograph documents the historical undertaking, not Centauri Archive personnel or a claim of affiliation with NASA. An original contributor portrait may be considered separately with documented informed consent.
